findings.title: The feature does not clear the confidence threshold because touched-module coverage evidence is still missing
evidence: `confidence_report.json` scores the slice at `0.83`, below the default `0.90` threshold.

The score penalty is entirely driven by `code_coverage = 0.0`; no coverage artifact exists under `pstf/features/SOUL_FACTORY_PROVISIONING_TRACKING/coverage/` or an equivalent location for the touched backend and web modules.

`verification_report.md` shows 14/14 ACs verified and 18/18 mapped tests passing, so this is not a behavior failure; it is an evidence-quality gap that the confidence model explicitly treats as release-significant.
findings.suggested_action: Either generate touched-module coverage evidence for the backend and browser suites or accept release explicitly as a risk exception rather than as a threshold-clearing approval.

proposed_hitl_question.question: The Soul Factory slice is behaviorally verified but still scores 0.83 because no touched-module coverage artifact exists. How should release proceed?
options: APPROVED_WITH_RISK — ship this slice and accept the missing coverage evidence as a documented release risk
NEEDS_WORK — require coverage artifacts before release approval
DEFERRED — do not decide release now; revisit after broader release planning
REJECTED — do not release this slice in its current state

findings.title: Soul Gallery stat cards hide zero values, which weakens operator visibility after live updates
evidence: During `web/tests/e2e/souls-gallery-live.spec.js`, the Suspended count disappeared after a live update drove the count to zero, which required the test to assert the updated cards indirectly rather than via an explicit `0` value.
`web/src/lib/components/Card.svelte` only renders the value block when `{#if value}` is truthy, so `0` is omitted entirely.
This follow-up is already tracked as beads issue `bahia-ijo8`.
findings.suggested_action: Render zero-valued card counts explicitly so live-update statistics remain visible to operators.

findings.title: Schema-backed validation for PSTF confidence and adversarial artifacts is still absent
evidence: The requested schema files `schemas/confidence_report.schema.json` and `schemas/adversarial_review.schema.json` are not present in the repository.
Both this review and the confidence report therefore rely on prompt-defined structure rather than repo-backed machine validation.
This does not invalidate the feature behavior, but it weakens repeatable artifact checking at release time.
findings.suggested_action: Add the missing PSTF schema files or document the canonical structures in-repo so future gate artifacts can be validated mechanically.
